author: TEDx Talks
description: Cultural strategist and Environmental activist, Daze Aghaji, believes that the multiple crises we’re living through – from the war in Palestine to the climate crisis to toxic gender debates – all stem from a crisis of belonging. As we search for belonging ‘hollow and unrooted ways’ like nationalism and anti-immigrant rhetoric seem to offer a solution. But Daze argues there are alternatives to these hollow solutions. She believes that culture can rebuild belonging to meaningfully address systemic political challenges because culture carries the values of our society and reminders of how we are meant to live together. By investing in our culture from folk carnivals to community gardens, we can co-create the culture needed to better belong to one another and our planet. Daze Aghaji is an environmentalist and cultural strategist whose work explores identity, belonging, and our relationship with the Earth. She co-founded Extinction Rebellion Youth, ran for election as the youngest MEP Cand
title: How to solve our crisis of belonging | Daze Aghaji | TEDxLondon

author: TEDx Talks
description: The manosphere has gone mainstream and its misogynistic teachings are now commonplace on and offline. Masculinity educator, Ben Hurst, has spent over a decade speaking to boys and young men about what it means to be a man and believes that conversations are key to combatting the manosphere’s harmful lessons. Using conversation models like ALEC (Asking, Listening, Encouraging and Checking in), Ben shows it’s possible to meet boys and young men where they’re at and help them rediscover what healthy masculinity looks like. Ben is an activist, advocate, speaker, host, facilitator, trainer and consultant. As the Director of Facilitation and Training at Beyond Equality, he focuses on deconstructing and reconstructing masculinities with men and boys. Ben is also the co-host of Climate Curious, a podcast for those who care about the world but find the current conversation about climate change confusing, scary or boring. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but i
title: How to talk to men and boys about the Manosphere  | Ben Hurst | TEDxLondon

author: TEDx Talks
description: One day, soprano, Gabriella Di Laccio, walked through a second hand book market and found two large encyclopaedias listing thousands of women composers throughout history. She was shocked - she had spent years studying music and never heard of these women composers. This was the beginning of Gabriella’s journey to find and share the forgotten history of women composers and their music. A journey that has become more urgent in the age of AI – datapoint by datapoint, composer by composer, Gabriella is determined to restore the missing half of humanity’s musical creativity.  Gabriella is a soprano and activist who brings to life the music and stories of the women history forgot. She founded the Donne Foundation to show how inequality shapes what we hear, amplifying the voices of women, past and present. In 2024, she led Let HER MUSIC Play: a 26-hour concert that broke a Guinness World Record uniting audiences across continents. Gabriella was also named one of the BBC’s 100 Most Inspiring
title: What AI learns when we erase women from music  | Gabriella Di Laccio | TEDxLondon

author: TEDx Talks
description: Descended from Amazonian and Andean healers and holding a PhD in chemical biology, Rosa Vásquez Espinoza bridges two worlds rarely seen together: Indigenous knowledge and modern science. Through her work protecting stingless bees in the Peruvian Amazon, Rosa shares a powerful story of how integrating science with Indigenous wisdom can help us protect nature and the planet more effectively. Rosa is a Peruvian chemical biologist, author, speaker, and National Geographic Explorer with Andean and Amazonian roots. Her work integrates traditional knowledge with modern science and technology to create solutions for our planet. Her discoveries have inspired new conservation policies and global awareness of Amazonian biodiversity. She was also named one of the BBC’s 100 Most Influential Women and was a recipient of Peru’s Order of Merit and the UNESCO-Al Fozan Prize (2025). This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Lea
title: Where Science Meets Ancestral Wisdom | Rosa Vásquez Espinoza | TEDxLondon

author: TEDx Talks
description: When Julia Middleton became a grandmother she felt pretty blasé about it. But it turns out being a working grandmother was a crash course in not only becoming a better leader, but also in becoming a better follower. For Julia, being a working grandmother has brought new mentors into her life - her grandchildren - and been a chance to keep learning about leadership. Julia is a best-selling author of If That’s Leading, I’m In, Leading beyond Authority and Cultural Intelligence and the host of the Women Emerging podcast. She is deeply committed to helping people from all backgrounds to lead. In 2024 she founded Women Emerging and now leads expeditions with women across the world. Prior to this Julia was Founder and Chief Executive of Common Purpose, which she grew to become one of the biggest leadership development organisations, globally. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.co
title: What grandmotherhood has taught me about leadership | Julia Middleton | TEDxLondon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
When criminal psychologist, Dr Julia Shaw, combed through thousands of green crime cases she found a common pattern, a psychological profile for the people committing environmental crimes. She calls them the ‘six pillars of environmental crime’: ease, impunity, greed, rationalisation, conformity, and desperation. These pillars can be applied across different types of green crimes, from corporate fraud, to organised crime, to cases of hit men hired to kill environmental defenders.

Understanding these pillars, and knocking them down one by one, Dr Shaw explains, is key to catching green criminals and preventing environmental crimes. In understanding the minds of the perpetrators we can map the key motivators of these criminals, and protect our planet.
 Dr Julia Shaw is a criminal psychologist who applies social science to some of the biggest issues of our time. She is a regular presenter of TV and audio programmes, including multiple series with the BBC. She is known for blending true
title: Inside the minds of green criminals | Julia Shaw | TEDxLondon

author: TEDx Talks
description: Civil engineer, Gemma Andrews, wants us to celebrate the quiet, invisible and dependable infrastructure that makes our lives easier – and is helping combat the effects of climate change. Using examples from around the world, such as smart motorways in Kuala Lumpur and clever cooling systems in Toronto, Gemma shows that the infrastructure we take for granted is protecting communities across the world. With the construction sector contributing around 30% to global carbon emissions, it’s more than important than ever that we build smart to protect people and the planet. A designer, builder, and problem-solver, Gemma is a Principal Civil Engineer with a career spanning large-scale energy, transport, and urban development projects. Gemma is an advocate for celebrating the unsung engineering marvels that create safe and sustainable societies, especially in the face of climate change. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local c
title: How invisible infrastructure is protecting people and planet | Gemma Andrews | TEDxLondon

author: TEDx Talks
description: Women’s crafts have often been dismissed as frivolous or meaningless, ignoring the stories and histories they hold within. Yet as medical student and women crafts enthusiast Nyneisha Bansal shows us, there is much more to crafts than meets the eye. Sharing stories from across history, the world and her family, Nyneisha shows how women's crafts have been used to build identity, shape society and pass down wisdom and heritage. Nyneisha is a third-year medical student at the University of Cambridge and her passion lies in the intersection between storytelling and craft. She was taught crochet by her great-grandmother who showed Nyneisha that handmade objects are vessels of memory and connection. She now crochets to raise awareness of how creativity can foster healing and bring people together. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The hidden stories behind women’s crafts | Nyneisha Bansal | TEDxLondon

author: TEDx Talks
description: What do you do when relationships in your workplace have broken down? It can feel impossible to repair the harm caused when relationships rupture. The good news is, shares harm repair specialist, Leah Brown, that there is a way forward. Using a four step approach from restorative justice, Leah shows it is possible to rebuild trust, heal relationships and create working harmony. Leah is a harm repair specialist, qualified solicitor and accredited mediator. She founded The WayFinders Group to repair the relational damage that fractures teams. Leah also hosts Address The Harm podcast centring survivor voices, and The Longest Day podcast, a weekly leadership podcast. She recently published the political white paper "From harm to healing: rebuilding trust in Britain's publicly funded institutions" and is spearheading a coalition on institutional accountability. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more a
title: How to repair harm in the workplace | Leah Brown | TEDxLondon

author: TEDx Talks
description: Imagine a thin, sensitive coating paper where everything that touches the surface leaves a trace. This is ‘Naturantypie’, an image-making technique developed by artist Maximilian Prüfer. It’s so sensitive that it can reveal the footprints of ants, the trails of snails and the moment rain lands on it. These normally invisible reminders of life are awe-inspiring and for Maxmilian a chance to celebrate nature and remind us to protect it - no matter how big or small.   Maximilian studied Design and Communication Strategy at HS Augsburg and Fine Arts at the Accademia di Belle Arti di Bologna in Italy. His work investigates natural processes and translates them into visual form, exploring existential and ecological questions about evolution and the relationship between humans and nature. A central element of his practice is Naturantypie, a technique he developed to record the movements and traces of insects as well as other natural phenomena. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TE
title: Naturantypie: a new art form inspired by nature | Maximilian Prüfer | TEDxLondon

author: TEDx Talks
description: Impacts of synthetic insulation on human health and the environment.   Delicia Gunn, FE, MPP is Founder & CEO of HEMPSULATION LLC. With a vision and desire to help reduce the construction industry’s carbon footprint while creating healthy living environments, Delicia launched HEMPSULATION in September 2021. Her debut product offering is a non-toxic, renewable insulation solution for walls, floors and ceilings that is good for the environment and better for human health. Under her leadership, HEMPSULATION has grown from an innovative idea to a viable product installed in residential and mixed-use buildings across the country. Delicia’s career in the construction industry began as a mechanical engineer designing green buildings and infrastructure projects. Her entrepreneurial spirit lead her to launch the consulting firm, Indigo Engineering Group, LLC, in 2004. Delicia holds a Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering from Howard University and a Master of Public Policy from America
title: The potential health effects of synthetic insulation | Delicia Gunn, FE, MPP | TEDxUStreetWomen

description: What if the very system designed to protect our health was also threatening it? In this deeply personal talk, an anesthesiologist invites us into the hidden world of hospitals - not just where lives are saved, but where unseen environmental costs quietly accumulate. Through compelling stories from both the operating room and the forest trail, she reveals a side of healthcare few have ever considered. This talk challenges us to rethink what it truly means to “do no harm.” It is a wake-up call for anyone who cares about human health and the planet we depend on. Anna Kšírová is a physician highlighting the links between climate change and health and healthcare. She graduated from the 2nd Medical Faculty of Charles University in Prague, after graduation she completed a several-month internship at the paediatric HIV clinic in Pretoria, South Africa, and currently works at the anaesthesiology and resuscitation department of Jablonec nad Nisou Hospital. She is a co-founding member of the Doc
title: The Hidden Climate Cost of Healthcare | Anna Kšírová | TEDxPrague

A comic songwriter turns thousands of social media comments into ironic songs, showing how even serious life stories can be transformed with humor and how sharing these moments online can become a wave of fracture that destabilizes, erodes, and generates new ways of looking at life.

description:
What if citizens were not just heard, but actually had the power to decide?
Participatory budgeting is changing how communities function, turning people from passive observers into active co-creators of their cities. It is not just about funding projects; it is about building trust, responsibility, and a shared sense of ownership.
In her talk, Ani Tovmasyan shares real stories from the field, highlighting both inspiring successes and the challenges that still stand in the way. Through her experience, we see how meaningful participation can reshape not only public spaces, but also the way people relate to their communities. Ani Tovmasyan is a sociologist and public relations specialist who has become one of the key contributors to the development of participatory budgeting culture in Armenia. title: From Voices to Decisions | Ani Tovmasyan | TEDxMoskovyanStSalon
